messages:
maya: seeing a big spike in TIME_WAIT counts on outbound NATs in us-west-2, looks correlated with a GPU node reboot wave after the nightly image refresh. model pulls failing with TLS handshake timeouts.
liam: ugh. which AZ? any specific host groups or instance types?
maya: az-a primarily, batch-gpu-rt pool. SYN/EST counters look fine but ephemeral port exhaustion is through the roof. kernel netstat: `tcp        0      0 10.0.2.15:34123       13.248.156.101:443     TIME_WAIT` repeated thousands.
ops-bot: alert: egress_port_pressure_high on nat-gw-a (instance id: nat-abc123) — 92% ephemeral allocation.
kevin: are model pulls using short-lived connections? our startup path currently does parallel pulls per GPU, ~8-12 per pod. that will blow ports.
sophia: yes, the node init script spins 12 concurrent curl downloads for weights + checksum verification. we assumed subnet scaling would absorb it.
maya: looks like the combination of rolling reboots + unchanged concurrency is the issue. requests pile into TIME_WAIT before kernel can reclaim.
liam: can we switch the init to reuse connections or add a local cache/proxy? maybe short-term: throttle concurrent pulls to 2 per pod during warmup.
kevin: i can push a hotfix to the bootstrap script to `--max-concurrency=2` and add exponential backoff for retries. will need a quick canary.
infra-oncall: Suggestion: failover traffic from nat-gw-a -> nat-gw-b while we roll the fix; also add ephemeral_port_reuse sysctl: `net.ipv4.tcp_tw_reuse=1` on the NAT instances as a short-term mitigation. note: check compliance with our TCP semantics.
sophia: can we also enable HTTP/2 multiplexing in the downloader to cut connections? that's low-risk and helpful longer-term.
maya: deploying `--max-concurrency=2` to canary (kube nodepool batch-gpu-rt-canary) now. will watch socket stats.
ops-bot: deploy started: maya/batch-bootpatch @ 3123456802
liam: FYI the runbook for ephemeral ports is at https://internal.redwood/runbooks/egress-ports — suggests three mitigations: reduce concurrency, add NAT capacity, reuse sockets via proxy.
kevin: canary applied, reduced failures from ~28% -> 4% on the canary nodes in 3 minutes. model pulls now serialized-ish.
maya: pushing the concurrency flag org-wide for the pool and scheduling a NAT capacity bump in the morning window. also planning to add a lightweight local proxy (squid-lite) on boot path to reuse connections.
infra-oncall: I'll open a ticket to provision additional NAT ENIs and attach them to nat-gw-a, and schedule a quick autoscaling policy review. ticket: INF-4821.
sophia: long-term action items: switch downloader to HTTP/2, add client-side connection pool, and make boot pulls consult a shared S3 warm cache per AZ.
liam: great. for immediate postmortem add: cause=concurrent model pulls during reboot wave, contributing=unchanged bootstrap concurrency, mitigations=throttle in bootstrap, nat capacity bump, sysctl reuse, future=http2+proxy+warm-cache.
maya: thanks all. monitoring shows TIME_WAIT counts dropping on canary NAT path. will keep thread updated and close after NAT capacity change and proxy rollout. :thumbsup:
ops-bot: incident status changed to mitigated @3123456835
